{{Short description|French mathematician}}
'''Henri Skoda''' (born 1945) is a French [[mathematician]], specializing in the analysis of [[several complex variables]].<ref>[http://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~henri.skoda/ Skoda's homepage]</ref>

Skoda studied from 1964 at l'[[École normale supérieure]] and received there in 1967 his [[agrégation]] in mathematics. He received in 1972 his Ph.D. from the [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis]] under [[André Martineau]] (primary advisor) and [[Pierre Lelong]] (secondary advisor) with thesis ''Étude quantitative des sous-ensembles analytiques de C<sup>n</sup> et des idéaux de functions holomorphes''.<ref>[http://www.idref.fr/031654924 ''Étude quantitative des sous-ensembles analytiques de C<sup>n</sup> et des idéaux de functions holomorphes''; Skoda, Henri - Notice documentaire IdRef]</ref> Skoda became a professor in Toulon and since 1976 has been a professor at the [[University of Paris VI]].

For many years he ran an analysis seminar with Pierre Lelong and [[Pierre Dolbeault]].

In 1978 Skoda received the [[Poncelet Prize]] and as an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Helsinki]] gave a talk ''Integral methods and zeros of holomorphic functions''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1978.2/Main/icm1978.2.0675.0684.ocr.pdf |title="Integral Methods and Zeros of Holomorphic Functions" by Henri Skoda, ICM 1978 |access-date=2015-10-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160927223243/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1978.2/Main/icm1978.2.0675.0684.ocr.pdf |archive-date=2016-09-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

His doctoral students include [[Jean-Pierre Demailly]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=107705}}</ref>
